descriptionChirho: A large watercraft, specifically Noah's ark in the flood narrative (Genesis 6-9). Translations consistently use vessel/ship terminology: Spanish 'arca' (ark), Arabic 'الفُلْكِ' (the ship/vessel), Hindi 'जहाज़' (ship), Korean '방주' (ark), Swahili 'safina' (ship/vessel from Arabic). The 26 occurrences all refer to the large boat built for the deluge, with prepositional forms 'in the ark' and construct forms showing various syntactic contexts but a single referent.

A small waterproof container or basket, specifically the reed basket in which the infant Moses was placed on the Nile (Exodus 2). Translations diverge sharply from the ark sense: Arabic 'سَفَطًا' (basket/chest, not فُلْك ship), Hindi 'टोकरी' (basket), Swahili 'sanduku' (box/chest, not safina/ship), English 'basket' (not ark). Spanish retains 'arca' but Korean shifts to '갈대의' (of reeds). Only 2 occurrences, both in the Moses infancy narrative, clearly a different-sized container from Noah's ark.
